C0.quote: likelihood of ties under positional scoring rules, edge-order-based rules
C0.note: Probability of ties under voting rules for random profiles; a property of voting procedures (indecisiveness).

C1.quote: We also complement the theoretical results by experiments on synthetic data
C1.note: Main results are probabilistic asymptotic characterisations of tie likelihood, which fit none of the listed types, so OT. Experiments on synthetic and Preflib data are secondary.

C2.1.quote: called a vote. The vector of n agents’ votes, denoted by P , is called a (preference) profile

C2.2.quote: Each agent uses a linear order to represent his or her preferences

C2.3.quote: agents’ “ground truth” preferences can be arbitrarily correlated and are chosen by an adversary
C2.3.note: Ground truth preferences are mentioned as a model feature.

C2.4.quote: and then independent noises are added to form their votes
C2.4.note: Ground-truth preferences are separate from the votes, which are generated by adding noise. The paper does not discuss strategic misreporting.

C3.1.note: No analysis considers strategic misreporting; votes are random draws.

C3.2.note: Votes are modelled as noisy versions of ground truth, not as sincere reports; no statement that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.note: No voter utility, welfare or satisfaction notions are used.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.note: Evaluates the likelihood of ties, not welfare or efficiency. Any welfare-related remarks, such as ties being desirable or undesirable, appear in the introduction.

VOT.note: Voters' votes are random draws from distributions and take no modelled action. The adversary picks distributions, not votes.

OTH.quote_behav: the max-adversary aims to maximize the likelihood of k-way ties
OTH.note: The adversary is an analytical device that chooses the distributions for the smoothed analysis (max- or min-adversary). It is not a voter. Its information is not discussed; it chooses the distributions directly, so complete information is inferred from the model.

C7.1.note: Fewer than two types are present.

C8.1.quote: the max-adversary aims to maximize the likelihood of k-way ties
C8.1.note: Only the adversary is strategic; it optimises distributions in a sup/inf formulation, which is a smoothed-analysis worst-case or best-case concept, not any listed solution concept.

claims.quote: so that the legislators can make an informed decision
a low max smoothed likelihood is good news
ties are not as rare as commonly believed, even in high-stakes elections

C9.1.note: Claims concern implications for real legislation and institutions.

C9.2.quote: Results in this paper characterize how rare this happens
C9.2.note: Applying the results to real elections requires that actual votes follow the smoothed model (strictly positive distributions). The text only partly supports this, and the paper admits Preflib differs from IC. The assumption that real electorates fit the model is not stated as such.

C10.1.note: The paper does not state a procedural reading.
